overviewHtml:
Attacks on Kubernetes often show up as small anomalies in audit logs, and alerts rarely reach the team that owns the workload.

What you get

  • A check every 10 minutes for potentially compromised service accounts, with an allow-list
  • Detection findings written to security.events
  • An instant workflow for new high and critical findings that finds the owners
  • A notification sub-workflow for email, Slack and Microsoft Teams
prereqsHtml:
• Dynatrace SaaS with Workflows
  • Kubernetes audit logs in Grail, for service account detection (see the use case documentation)
  • Permission for the workflow to ingest into security.events
  • Slack, Microsoft Teams and/or Email for Workflows, for notifications
  • Ownership teams on your Kubernetes workloads
setupHtml:
1. In Workflows, choose Upload and import notification-sender-sub-workflow.workflow-template.yaml first. Assign the notification connections.
  2. Import critical-finding-instant-notification.workflow-template.yaml and replace ` in trigger_notification_sender` with the sender's ID.
  3. Import service-account-unauthorized-access.workflow-template.yaml.
  4. Run each one manually once, then activate the triggers.
getStartedHtml:
You need Dynatrace Workflows, Kubernetes audit logs in Grail and ownership teams on your workloads.

  1. Import the notification sender sub-workflow first
  2. Import the finding notification and detection workflows
  3. Link them, run each once, then activate the triggers
